solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Photographer I hesitate to say cut some wire

parts.note: a pap is tabloid slang for a paparazzo, a celebrity-chasing cameraman
er is the noise of someone hesitating before speaking
to clip is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A cameraman reluctantly admits to snipping some wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent loop of steel for holding sheets together is a small piece of wire.

clue.text: Dignitary and I see fool making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction, upwards in this down light

parts.note: ah is what you say when you see the point
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A grandee and the speaker watch an idiot return.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official, so a person of rank and importance.

clue.text: Pressure on business and finance area to show rapid development

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means on or concerning
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Pressure on companies and the financial district produces a boom.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocity is early or unusually fast maturing, especially in a child's abilities.

clue.text: Give another order to bring up compass

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
compass in the sense of scope or extent is range

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise a navigation instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To give things another order is to put them into a new sequence or layout.

clue.text: Drunk feeling of Parisian twirling in sparkly pair of capes

parts.note: light can mean bright or sparkling, as in light eyes or a light wine

indicators.note: in tells us the turned French word goes inside the run of other pieces

parts.note: a head and a ness are both words for a headland or cape

indicators.note: twirling turns the little French word round so it reads the other way

parts.note: de is French, a Parisian's word, for of

explanation.surface: A tipsy sensation in a Frenchman spinning in glittery cloaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capes' look like cloaks but are headlands, and 'sparkly' is not the drunk's wine but bright, as in light.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dizzy and giddy is the state brought on by too much alcohol.

clue.text: Rocky pass, with one circling safe place to walk

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mountain pass where a lone walker goes round in circles to stay safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' shuffles PASS, ONE and CIRCLING; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls by pressing a button.

clue.text: Bashes in gent's face, regrettably

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so just its opening letter

parts.note: alas is said regretfully

explanation.surface: Someone punches a man in the face and is sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bashes' looks like a verb of violence, but it is the informal noun for parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is slang for a party, and galas are festive celebrations.

clue.text: Dance music performance on unicycle's frame

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A band plays dance music while someone shows off on a unicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigue is a lively baroque dance, often the closing movement of a suite, like a jig.

clue.text: Overweight, mostly love taking it steady

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: large is a polite word for overweight
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A heavy lover is advised to take things slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo, so playing at an unhurried pace.

clue.text: Rogue American star inhales oxygen and no smoke

indicators.note: something inhaled is drawn inside, so the star surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
fag is British slang for a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: A disreputable US celebrity breathes oxygen and gives up cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' belongs to the definition: the phrase is chiefly US slang. 'star' looks like the celebrity but is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Son of a gun is an American slang term for a rascal, used jokily or with affection.

clue.text: Report on woman's affair

indicators.note: in an across light, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
a report is a loud noise, such as a bang

explanation.surface: A news story about a woman's love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance but means a business or set of things, as in the whole shebang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang means an affair or matter, almost always in the idiom the whole shebang.

clue.text: Working girl, one showing restraint

indicators.note: working means being worked on, kneaded into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A working girl, a woman showing self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a shackle fastened round a prisoner's ankle to restrain movement.

clue.text: American and British close relationship

parts.note: to a British setter writing for British solvers, something British is ours

explanation.surface: The special relationship between the USA and Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British' gives OUR because the setter and his paper are British; 'and' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, especially a secret one: an intimate bond between two people.

clue.text: Swell clothing naughty wife's cast off, having dressed down

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the swell surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a swell is an upper-class dandy, a toff

indicators.note: cast off means thrown away, so the letter for wife is dropped

parts.note: wicked means naughty
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A dandy wearing his wicked wife's discarded clothes, rather underdressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast off' drops W from WICKED, leaving ICKED. 'Swell' is not a wave but a toff, a British word for a posh man.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off and to dress down both mean to reprimand someone sharply.

clue.text: Put on coat for investigating in marsh

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the wetland word

parts.note: a fen is a marsh, especially in eastern England

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A detective dons a coat to search a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like dressing, matching 'coat', but it means pretend.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on is to fake it, to pretend or simulate it.

clue.text: Lie in a university hospital, digging into nosh

indicators.note: digging into means burrowing inside, so the pieces go inside the word for nosh

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food
the LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient at a university hospital tucking into a meal tells a fib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digging into' makes 'nosh' read as eating, but it encloses the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth or a statement known to be untrue is simply a deliberate fib.

clue.text: Honouring good maid, holding nothing back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse
holding means containing, so the zero goes between the other pieces

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid, a word also used in English
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Giving an award to a fine housemaid who never holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: BONNE, French for a maid, is used in English for a housemaid; 'back' reverses everything once the zero is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage, the ultimate honour.

clue.text: Digs patch of earth, given great chance

parts.note: a flower bed is a patch of earth
in sport a sitter is an easy chance that should be taken

explanation.surface: A gardener digs a plot and hopes for a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is not the verb but British slang for lodgings; a sitter is a sporting chance too easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat is a typical student's lodgings, informally called digs in Britain.

clue.text: Echoing musical notes ascending

indicators.note: ascending means going up, so in this down light the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
ti and mi are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Notes of a tune rising and resounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing someone means copying or mimicking them, repeating what they did.

clue.text: Boss drinking port who carries out some services

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the port goes inside the boss

parts.note: a leader is a boss
Ayr is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A boss downing port while working as a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, matching 'drinking', but it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-ordained church member licensed to lead certain services is one who conducts worship.

clue.text: Spirits, or one that's picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: one spirit, a drink, is gin

explanation.surface: Choosing drinks: spirits, or something you collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'Spirits': gin is one spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are supernatural beings of Arabic folklore, spirits that can take human or animal form.

clue.text: Side ripe for transformation welcoming United's playmaker

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the letter for United goes inside the jumbled letters
letters up for transformation are to be rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A football side ready for a shake-up signs Manchester United's midfield creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playmaker' is a football term but here means a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the great tragedians of ancient Athens, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Itinerant person moving stock loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a drover drives cattle or sheep, moving livestock to market

explanation.surface: A travelling cattle driver gets decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home, a person who travels about, is an itinerant.

clue.text: Analyse almost astronomical distance

indicators.note: almost means nearly all of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a parsec is a unit of astronomical distance, about 3.26 light years

explanation.surface: Someone studies a near-cosmic length.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to analyse it into its grammatical parts.

clue.text: Two places to save a designated victim

parts.note: the phrase as a whole names two places to put savings; the first is an ISA, a British tax-free Individual Savings Account
the second place to save is an AC, the usual abbreviation for an account

explanation.surface: Two spots in which to rescue a marked man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like rescue but means put money by. An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham's son was chosen as the sacrifice until an angel stayed his father's hand.

clue.text: Half-heartedly pamper mathematicians' group

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, one of the two middle letters is dropped

parts.note: to cosset is to pamper

explanation.surface: Mathematicians grudgingly spoiling a team.
explanation.definitionFit: In group theory a coset is a subgroup shifted by one fixed element, a set mathematicians work with.

clue.text: Heads round front of battle lines

parts.note: a round thing is O-shaped

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: A general leads troops around the front line of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' sounds like leaders, but it is the side of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin is the side bearing the head, the face called heads.

clue.text: Senses cool temperature in pants suit

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: in puts the temperature letter inside the jumbled letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess

explanation.surface: Feeling a chill while wearing a trouser suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' jumbles SUIT, and 'in' places T inside, giving TUITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to know it by instinct, to sense it without reasoning.

clue.text: Lament online network going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in email
a grid is a network, as of power lines

explanation.surface: Bemoaning an internet system that is headed in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or hymn for the dead, a lament.

clue.text: Fat guards not quite clothed providing foodstuff

indicators.note: guards means surrounding protectively, so the fat wraps round the other piece

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is missing

parts.note: garbed means dressed or clothed

explanation.surface: Overweight sentries barely dressed supply the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like an adjective for the guards but is the noun, kidney fat used in British puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a crop grown for its sugar-rich root, refined into table sugar.
